newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast desalination centre established in Oman.
newsitem.headline: Mideast desalination centre established in Oman.

text.p: An agreement establishing a multi-million-dollar research centre on water desalination in the Middle East was signed in the Omani capital Muscat this week, sources close to the project said.
The Middle East Desalination Centre is one of many projects spawned by the Middle East peace process.
The United States, Japan, Oman and Israel have granted the centre $3 million each, while South Korea has contributed $600,000, the sources said.
The European Union is planning to donate some $3.6 million, the sources added.

The Muscat-based centre will carry out studies on regional water resources, desalination and related technology. Water -- a scarce resource in the Middle East -- is a bitter point of contention between Israelis and Palestinians as well as between other states in the region.

Oman, which along with Qatar has gone further than all other Gulf Arab states to establish links with Israel, froze ties with the Jewish state earlier this month. Oman says Israel is not adhering to its commitments to the Palestinian leadership. Qatar has also put its ties with Israel on hold for similar reasons.
No figures for the centre's annual budget were immediately available.
